question: Within the frozen two-stage retrieval-competition learner, can any attenuation of the four verified terminal bonuses reach the registered 0.02 F1 gain on the measured 91-question training factorial? Keep the raw four-path values and previously screened root effects fixed. This is a capacity diagnostic only; do not use its optimistic choices as an actor.
bound: Allow independent attenuation between zero and one for every original signed terminal comparison, including the fourth comparison with no observed terminal heading. Center and scale the features and use the exact donor ridge penalty. Use signed linear prediction weights to bound an outer and every required inner terminal probability. Bound each root training target over the two donor-held terminal probability ranges including the piecewise-affine common-suffix credit; include diagonal intersections as well as rectangle corners. Apply the signed ridge weights to enclose the root probability. Within each unseen dialogue's window, optimize the measured question-mean return over the corners of the three probability intervals. This relaxation permits more choices than a single deployable credit assignment. Weight windows by the number of original questions.
checks: The all-retained point must reproduce all stored held-out probabilities and F1. Verify both point intervals and the inclusion of every corner of the four-label attenuation cube using exact shared-retention fits. Also report the largest observed vertex F1 separately. Use the interval upper bound, not a vertex maximization, for a negative capacity conclusion.
